notes:
CIRCUIT: a 100V source (#4) on the left vertical (x~176) drives a 5Ohm series resistor (#0) on the top rail (y~372); to the right of the resistor the top rail runs unbroken to x~720 and feeds three parallel shunt branches that all return to the bottom rail (y~583): 1kOhm resistor (#2) at x~430, 25H inductor (#1) at x~588, and 2F capacitor (#3) at x~721. The 1k branch's vertical continues through the bottom rail down to the GND symbol (#5) at (429,623).

NET MAP (3 nets, 6 components):
  0  = the bottom rail y~583 from x~176 to x~721, the stub below it down to GND, and the lower legs of all three shunt branches. Terminals: 4.1 (bottom of the 100V source), 2.1 (bottom of the 1k), 1.1 (bottom of the 25H), 3.1 (bottom plate lead of the 2F cap), 5.0 (GND).
  n1 = top rail left of the 5Ohm (x~176-243) down the left vertical to the top terminal of the 100V source: 0.0, 4.0.
  n2 = top rail right of the 5Ohm (x~333-720) plus the three vertical stubs down to the tops of the shunt branches: 0.1, 2.0, 1.0, 3.0.

JUDGEMENT CALLS / SITE DECISIONS (all three CRITICAL sites plus the CRITICAL gap bridge inspected):
  S0 (582,374) -> JUNCTION. Clean T: the top rail runs through horizontally and a single vertical stub drops from it to the top of the 25H inductor. deg=3, no hop, no ink above the rail. Reading it as anything but a junction would strand the inductor's top on a one-terminal net and leave the inductor with no path to the source.
  S11 (588,581) -> JUNCTION. Clean T where the inductor's lower lead lands on the bottom rail. Not joining would strand 1.1 alone and give the inductor branch no return.
  S13 (427,584) -> JUNCTION. Here the 1k branch's vertical crosses the bottom rail and continues below it to the GND symbol; deg=4, hop metric 3.6 which is noise, no jog and no semicircle in the crop. Junction is what makes the bottom rail net '0'. The crossing reading would split this into (bottom rail + source bottom + inductor bottom + cap bottom) and (1k bottom + GND) as two separate nets: the 1k would then be a dead-end branch carrying no current and the rest of the circuit would float with no ground reference. That is the electrically impossible reading, so junction wins on rule 1.
  B0 gap bridge (436,371)<->(430,372), flagged CRITICAL: KEPT (not dropped). An inkmap dump at (432,374) shows the top rail is solid ink from x=417 to x=431 and again from x=436 to x=452 on rows 370-372, with only a 4-pixel dropout at x=432-435 - a pen-lift/scan dropout inside one straight stroke, not a deliberate break (the drafter draws no hop or jog there, and the stroke resumes at exactly the same y). Dropping the bridge would cut the top rail immediately right of the 1k tap, leaving the 25H and 2F tops on a net whose only other members are their own top leads - a disconnected island with no source and no return path. Rule 1 (electrical impossibility) settles it: keep the bridge.

NON-CRITICAL SITES (left at tracer default, none change the netlist): S2 and S8 are the handwritten '2F' label ink touching the capacitor's leads; S3, S4 and S6 are the '25H' label ink touching the inductor coil; S9 and S10 are the '1kOhm' label ink touching the resistor. All are text-to-symbol contacts, not wire-to-wire.
